summary: Both sides now render a genuinely static, index-driven field of full-value random colors with uniform hue; the only divergence is saturation mix — the original rails ~58% of pixels at full saturation while the port rails only ~16%, so the port reads noticeably more pastel and ~9% brighter.
observations: RE-JUDGE CONFIRMS THE ENGINE FIX: the original no longer renders solid hue-0 red. Both sides now render a field of per-pixel random colors. Provenance of all runs: portSha256 a81c4ea9c8ef, epeSha256 df48de8460fc, harnessSha256 40eb475a94b8.

TRULY STATIC on both sides. motion avg/min/max = 0 and motionLit = 0 with zeroMotionFrames = 300/300 over the 60 s survey (5 fps) and 480/480 over a 240 s survey (2 fps); meanBrightness min == max == first == last, brightnessTrend 'steady' on both. Dumps at t=300 s, t=303 s and t=305.9 s (--skip 300, 600 px) are BYTE-IDENTICAL to each other AND byte-identical to the t=0 dump of the same seed/rig on both sides. The field is fixed at init and never moves.
CONTROL SURFACE MATCHES: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for BOTH sides. No dials to compare.

BOTH SIDES ARE INDEX-ONLY AND GEOMETRY-INDEPENDENT, identically so. Pixel i's color depends only on i, never on the rig: at seed 1 the 60 px strip frame is a byte-exact prefix of the 600 px strip frame, of the 8x8 grid frame (flattened), of the 32x8 grid frame, and of the 5x5x5-ish cloud frame; the 7 px frame is a byte-exact prefix of the 60 px frame. True on orig and on port. So the port reproduces the original's stream/prefix structure exactly.
BOTH SIDES: VALUE IS ALWAYS EXACTLY 1.0. Over 20,000 pooled pixels (5 seeds x 4000 px) every single pixel has max channel = 255 on both sides. No brightness randomness on either side.

BOTH SIDES: HUE IS UNIFORM ON [0,1). Pooled 20-bin hue histograms (n=20,000, 5% expected per bin): orig 5.30 4.92 5.12 5.13 5.17 5.18 4.90 5.00 5.09 4.83 5.07 5.04 4.83 4.71 4.86 4.94 5.00 4.92 5.07 4.93; port 4.97 5.25 5.08 4.85 4.83 5.21 4.92 4.92 4.98 4.98 5.00 4.96 5.06 5.11 5.08 5.18 4.95 4.77 5.08 4.81. Both flat within sampling noise. corr(hue,sat) ~0 on both (0.0025 / 0.0055); lag-1 autocorrelation of hue and of saturation ~0 on both. Colors are i.i.d. per pixel on both sides.

THE ONE DIVERGENCE — FRACTION OF FULLY-SATURATED PIXELS. Because value is always 1, saturation reads exactly off the minimum channel (s = (255-min)/255; s == 1 iff some channel is 0). Pooled over 20,000 pixels: orig P(s == 1) = 58.22%, port P(s == 1) = 16.14%. Mean saturation orig 0.8776 vs port 0.7556.

The divergence is stable across well-separated seeds, not a one-seed fluke. Per-seed P(s==1) at 600 px — seed 1: orig 60.7% / port 17.2%; seed 7: 57.7% / 15.0%; seed 1234: 59.7% / 16.8%; seed 99999: 57.7% / 18.2%. Pooled 4000 px runs at seeds 11/222/3333/44444/555555 give the same 58% vs 16%.

THE NON-RAILED PART OF THE SATURATION DISTRIBUTION IS IDENTICAL. Conditional CDF of saturation given s < 1, pooled n=20,000, evaluated at s = .1 .2 .3 .4 .5 .6 .7 .8 .9 .95 — orig: 3.77 8.08 12.79 18.14 24.18 31.09 39.01 49.18 63.23 74.36; port: 3.96 8.12 12.71 18.02 23.77 30.82 38.51 49.11 63.16 74.52. Agreement within +-0.5 percentage points at every point; conditional means 0.6926 (orig) vs 0.6945 (port). So the two sides draw the SAME sub-1 saturation shape and differ ONLY in how much probability mass lands on the s == 1 rail.

Downstream effect on brightness: mean brightness orig 143-146 vs port 155-160 across every run (60 px strip, 600 px strip, 4000 px strip, 8x8 and 32x8 grids, cloud). The ~9-11% gap is entirely explained by the port having fewer zero-channel (fully saturated) pixels.

VISUAL CHARACTER: at 60 px both are static vertical stripes of saturated neon colors. The original's stripes are predominantly pure hues (pure blue, pure magenta, pure cyan, pure green, with occasional pastels); the port mixes in visibly more washed-out/pastel stripes (salmon, peach, pale blue, pale pink). Distinct unique-color counts at 600 px: orig 561/600, port 597/600 (the original repeats colors more because so many pixels sit on the fully-saturated rail).
Both sides are seed-responsive: dumps at seeds 1, 7, 1234, 99999 differ from each other on both sides (no side ignores --seed).
wantsSensors: false on both sides; sensors fed: 'off' on both. No compile or runtime errors on either side in any run. meta.json warnings arrays empty throughout.
feedback: The ONLY thing to fix is the fraction of pixels that come out fully saturated. Target: ~58% of pixels should have a zero color channel (pure hue at full value). The port currently produces ~16%. Everything else — staticness, hue uniformity, always-full value, per-pixel independence, index-only prefix-stable stream, seed responsiveness, empty control surface — already matches the original exactly.

Do NOT change the shape of the non-saturated tail: measured conditional on s < 1, the two sides' saturation distributions are already identical to within +-0.5 percentage points (conditional CDF at s = .1/.3/.5/.7/.9 is orig 3.8/12.8/24.2/39.0/63.2 vs port 4.0/12.7/23.8/38.5/63.2). A naive rescale or offset of the saturation draw would raise the rail mass but destroy that agreement. The two sides look like the same sub-1 draw mixed with a 'fully saturated' branch that fires at different rates (~58% orig vs ~16% port) — raise the port's rail rate while leaving the sub-1 draw alone.

Verification target for a fix pass: render 4000 px at several seeds, compute s = (255 - min(r,g,b))/255 per pixel, and check (a) P(s == 1) lands near 0.58, (b) the conditional CDF given s < 1 stays within a point or two of the orig table above, (c) mean brightness drops from ~157 to ~144.
No other axis needs work: the field is byte-stable from t=0 to t=306 s on both sides, both are byte-identical across strip/grid/cloud rigs for the same pixel index, and both expose zero controls.
